title: App versions from user agents
prompt: The mobile team wants to know which app versions are calling the API. Write `solve(api_requests)` with RDD functions so it returns, for every request made by our apps, the `request_id`, the `platform` and the `app_version`.
rules: A request comes from our apps when its `user_agent` starts with exactly `RuntimeShop-`, such as `RuntimeShop-iOS/4.12.0 (iPhone; iOS 17.5)`. Skip every other request, including those with no user agent.
`platform` is the text between `RuntimeShop-` and the first `/` (`iOS`); `app_version` is the text after that `/`, up to the first space or the end (`4.12.0`).
Keep repeated requests. Return `request_id`, `platform` and `app_version`, all text, in that order. An empty table gives an empty result.
hints: Use `api_requests.rdd.filter(...)` with a named function that checks the user agent, then `map` each row to a tuple.
A missing user agent arrives as `None`, and `None.startswith(...)` raises. Check for `None` first.
Plain Python does the parsing: cut off the prefix, `split("/", 1)`, then keep the part before the first space. Finish with `toDF("request_id string, ...")`.
explanation: Filter with a function that returns `agent is not None and agent.startswith("RuntimeShop-")`, then map each row to `(request_id, platform, version)`, where the agent without its prefix is split once on `/` and the version is cut at the first space. `toDF` with a schema string gives the column names and types, and works even when no request matches; with names only it fails on an empty RDD. Testing `"RuntimeShop" in agent` without the `None` check stops the job on a request with no user agent.
